issues.description: Renaming `audio_packet_bytes` to `fixed_audio_packet_size` is a breaking API change with no deprecation shim
issues.detail: The changelog states the field was renamed from `audio_packet_bytes` to `fixed_audio_packet_size`, but the diff to `FastAPIWebsocketParams` only adds the new field — there is no backward-compat alias, no Pydantic validator emitting a DeprecationWarning, and no migration note. Any existing user passing `audio_packet_bytes=...` will get a Pydantic validation error (or silently ignored field, depending on model config). For a public transport param this should either keep the old name as a deprecated alias for at least one minor release or be called out as a breaking change in the changelog.

issues.description: Fixed-size packetization bypasses pacing / `_next_send_time`, breaking real-time audio framing it claims to provide
issues.detail: The PR description says the feature provides 'real-time pacing' for endpoints like Vonage Audio Connector, but `_write_frame` calls `self._client.send(chunk)` in a tight `while` loop with no awaiting of `_next_send_time` and no sleep between chunks. If the serializer emits a large buffer (e.g. a TTS chunk covering 200ms), the loop will dump ten 20ms packets back-to-back at wire speed, which is exactly what real-time media endpoints reject. The `_send_interval`/`_next_send_time` mechanism that the rest of the class uses for pacing is not invoked here.

issues.description: Residual audio in `_audio_send_buffer` is never flushed or zero-padded at end-of-stream
issues.detail: When the stream ends (EndFrame, cancellation, or connection close), any leftover bytes shorter than `fixed_audio_packet_size` stay in `_audio_send_buffer` and are silently dropped. For Vonage and similar endpoints this means the trailing tail of the last utterance is truncated. The code should either flush a final zero-padded packet on EndFrame/disconnect or log a warning; today it is silent data loss.

issues.description: Packetization only inspects the immediate `payload` type, not the source frame — non-audio bytes payloads get chunked too
issues.detail: The branch is entered when `payload` is `bytes`/`bytearray`, regardless of whether the originating frame was an `AudioRawFrame`. If a serializer ever returns binary for a non-audio frame (e.g. a binary control message, protobuf, or image), it will be sliced into PCM-sized chunks and corrupted. The check should be gated on `isinstance(frame, AudioRawFrame)` rather than the payload type.

issues.description: Vonage serializer ignores `vonage_sample_rate` when deserializing if `setup()` is never called
issues.detail: `self._sample_rate` is initialized to `0` and only set in `setup()`. If `deserialize` is invoked before `setup()` (e.g. a stray inbound frame during reconnect, or a misuse), `_input_resampler.resample(..., self._sample_rate)` will be called with target rate `0`, producing undefined behavior or a divide-by-zero deep in the resampler. A guard or a sane default (e.g. `vonage_sample_rate`) would harden this.

issues.description: `_write_frame` early-returns after the packetization branch and skips the trailing `self._client.send(payload)` path — but also skips any future logic added below
issues.detail: The `return` inside the packetization block is correct for now, but the structure means any future logic added after the `if payload:` block (e.g. metrics, logging, post-send hooks) will silently not run when `fixed_audio_packet_size` is enabled. Refactoring to a single send path that conditionally splits would be more robust. Minor structural risk.

issues.description: DTMF parsing accepts both `digit` and `dtmf.digit` shapes with no documented source
issues.detail: The comment says 'Vonage may send digit in different formats, try both', but the Vonage Audio Connector docs define a single shape. Either link to the doc justifying both shapes, or pick one and validate. As written, it looks like defensive guessing.

issues.description: Copyright header says `2024–2025` on a new 2026 file
issues.detail: New file `src/pipecat/serializers/vonage.py` is added in 2026 but carries `Copyright (c) 2024–2025, Daily`. Trivial, but pipecat's other files typically extend the range to the current year on new additions.

issues.description: No unit tests added for the new serializer or the packetization path
issues.detail: Both the serializer (with its resampler interactions, DTMF parsing, and JSON event dispatch) and the new `fixed_audio_packet_size` chunking in the transport are non-trivial and entirely untested in the diff. At minimum, table-driven tests for: serialize(AudioRawFrame) sizing, deserialize(bytes), DTMF event parsing, and the chunk/remainder logic in `_write_frame` would catch the issues above.

issues.description: `vonage_sample_rate` field allows arbitrary ints with no validation
issues.detail: `InputParams.vonage_sample_rate: int = 16000` accepts any int including 0 or negative. The docstring lists allowed values (8000/16000/24000); a Pydantic `Literal[8000, 16000, 24000]` or a validator would prevent misconfiguration that surfaces later as resampler errors.

dissents.topic: Whether the rename of `audio_packet_bytes` is actually breaking

positions.position: Renames of public API fields without a deprecation alias are breaking and must be P0 — users have config files / code referencing the old name today.

If `audio_packet_bytes` was never released (i.e. only existed on main between two unreleased commits), the rename is harmless and the changelog note is sufficient. Verifying release history would downgrade this to P2.

dissents.topic: Whether the packetization loop needs explicit pacing

positions.position: Real-time audio endpoints require wall-clock pacing; sending ten 20ms packets in one tick violates the protocol contract regardless of what the receiver tolerates in practice — this is P1.
Vonage and most WebSocket audio endpoints buffer aggressively; pacing is typically handled upstream by the audio source rate. Calling this a P1 may be overcautious — P2 with a note is enough.

dissents.topic: Whether residual buffer flushing is a real bug

positions.position: Any code that buffers partial state must define drain semantics. Silent truncation at EOS is a correctness bug.
For PCM streams the final ≤20ms tail is inaudible; adding flush plumbing across EndFrame/cancel paths is more complexity than the bug warrants. Document and move on.

review.summary: The PR adds a clean, focused Vonage Audio Connector serializer and an optional fixed-size packetization buffer on the FastAPI WebSocket transport. The serializer is straightforward but lacks tests, has a soft initialization assumption (`_sample_rate=0` until `setup()`), and uses defensive DTMF shape-guessing without doc justification. The transport change is the riskier surface: the new packetization path keys off payload type rather than frame type (could corrupt non-audio binary), never flushes the residual buffer at end-of-stream (silent tail truncation), and doesn't engage the existing `_next_send_time` pacing despite the PR claiming real-time pacing as a goal. The `audio_packet_bytes` → `fixed_audio_packet_size` rename is also flagged in the changelog but has no compatibility shim, which is breaking if the old name shipped. Recommend addressing the gating-by-frame-type, EOS flush, and rename compatibility before merge; tests and pacing are strong follow-ups.
